title: Remember settings for tray widgets that are disabled and later re-enabled
line: System Tray widgets that you disable and enable again now keep their settings.
explanation: When an entry was set to "Never show (disabled)" in the System Tray settings, the tray deleted the widget's whole config group and forgot its id. Enabling it again created a brand new applet with default settings. The change only deletes the running applet and keeps its config group and id, so re-enabling (now or after a restart) loads the old applet id with its settings, the same path already used for widgets that come and go with their D-Bus service.

commits.message:
applets/systemtray: keep the settings of disabled tray widgets

Disabling a widget in the System Tray settings deleted its config group,
so enabling it again created a fresh applet with default settings. Keep
the config group and its id instead, so the widget comes back as it was.

BUG: 452599

media.caption: Master: Lock Keys configured to show Num Lock only
Master: after disabling and re-enabling Lock Keys in the tray settings, it is back to the defaults (Caps Lock)
With the fix: Lock Keys configured to show Num Lock only
With the fix: after disabling and re-enabling Lock Keys, Num Lock only is kept

review.text: Fixes the exact root cause in SystemTray::onEnabledAppletsChanged() by keeping the disabled applet's config group and m_configGroupIds entry while still deleting the running applet instance, matching stopApplet(). This cleanly integrates with SystemTray::restoreContents() and startApplet() both within a session and across plasmashell restarts, leaves uninstalled/invalid plugin cleanup intact, and passes systemtraymodeltest.

reviews.text: Fixes the exact root cause in SystemTray::onEnabledAppletsChanged() by keeping the disabled applet's config group and m_configGroupIds entry while still deleting the running applet instance, matching stopApplet(). This cleanly integrates with SystemTray::restoreContents() and startApplet() both within a session and across plasmashell restarts, leaves uninstalled/invalid plugin cleanup intact, and passes systemtraymodeltest.

Dropping the deleteGroup() and the m_configGroupIds removal makes disabling a tray widget behave like stopApplet() does for D-Bus-activated widgets: the applet is deleted (non-transient, so libplasma keeps its config) and startApplet() later recycles the same id, which is exactly what the reporter asked for. The tray's own restoreContents only caches ids and never loads applets by itself, so a kept group for a disabled widget doesn't resurrect it at startup, which the restart check in verify confirms. The before/after Lock Keys screenshots prove the settings are kept, and the commit message matches the 1-line diff; the only nit is that a disabled widget that is later uninstalled leaves a small orphan group in appletsrc.
